Your form has been submitted successfully' screen; form status flipped to 'received' with attachment; staff GET /api/forms/{id}/download returned 200/26 bytes/application/octet-stream/nosniff. critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/settings.py PUT /settings is behind require_roles('doctor','nurse','psychologist') and relies on the implicit admin bypass inside require_roles for admin access. This is correct but non-obvious; consider adding 'admin' to the explicit list for readability and to protect against future refactors of require_roles that could drop the bypass.

forms.py public_upload_back has no rate limiting or CAPTCHA — the public token is the only guard. If a token leaks, an attacker can spam 15MB uploads until storage fills. Consider (a) tracking upload attempts per token, or (b) blocking upload after status='received'.

forms.py public_upload_back overwrites any prior attachment silently (no history). If a patient uploads twice, the first file is orphaned in object storage. Consider keeping a history array or refusing second upload with 400.

SettingsInput.whatsapp accepts any string with no length/format validation. A user could paste 10KB of text into whatsapp and it would persist. Add max_length constraint (e.g. 40 chars) and optional regex.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (whatsapp header persistence, 3/3 template downloads, whatsapp row button opens wa.me, public upload-back → staff download all verified)
